material: Recycled-yarn Performance Loop band with polymer sensor module
features: Screenless — every reading lives in the Google Health app
24/7 heart rate, HRV, SpO2 and skin-temperature sensing
AFib alerts from the optical sensor (no ECG electrodes)
5 minutes on the charger buys a full day of use
12g with the fabric loop band fitted

specs.gpsType: None — no GPS chip. Distance, pace and route come from the paired phone, so no phone means no route
specs.displayType: None — screenless; there is no way to read a metric off the band itself
specs.batteryAssumptions: Google claims 'up to one week'. Continuous HR and SpO2 are on by default; there is no always-on display to switch off. Full charge ~90 minutes; a 5-minute top-up gives one day
specs.subscriptionModel: Optional but the AI half is gated — Google Health Coach (adaptive plans, AI sleep-trend analysis) needs Google Health Premium. Heart rate, sleep stages, recovery guidance and women's health tracking are free. 3-month trial in the box
specs.waterRating: Not published in Google's launch materials — the bands are described only as 'sweatproof, wetproof silicone'
specs.ecgAfibStatus: AFib alerts from the PPG sensor. No ECG electrodes, so no on-demand ECG at any price
specs.spo2Sensor: Yes — dedicated red and infrared SpO2 sensors
specs.chargerType: Proprietary magnetic contact charger — lose it and only Google sells the replacement
specs.dataExport: Google Takeout export of the Google Health/Fitbit archive (JSON and CSV bundles)

pros: $99.99 buys the whole feature set — unlike Whoop there is no membership standing between you and the hardware
Tom's Guide measured a full 7 days with 15% left after a dozen workouts
Heart rate held up against Garmin's entry-level watch in independent side-by-side testing
5-minute charge for a day of use removes the usual 'flat band, lost night of sleep data' problem
cons: No GPS chip and no screen: leave your phone behind on a run and you get no route, no pace and nothing to glance at
Google Health Coach — the AI coaching the launch was built around — costs $9.99/month or $99.99/year after the 3-month trial
Replacement bands start at $34.99 from Google and no third-party straps have appeared yet
Auto-detection needs 15+ minutes of activity, and only 41 exercise modes are supported
Google does not publish a water-resistance rating for the device in its launch materials
shortTagline: The $99 screenless Fitbit — great value, but no phone means no route and no screen.

material: Aluminium case with Gorilla Glass 3 and flexible silicone band
features: Built-in GPS + GLONASS — the only Fitbit band that maps a run without a phone
Heart-rate broadcast to gym equipment and Peloton over Bluetooth
ECG and EDA electrical sensors on the case sides
Google Maps directions and Google Wallet on the wrist
Small and large bands both included in the box

specs.gpsType: Built-in GPS + GLONASS — works with the phone left at home
specs.displayType: AMOLED colour touchscreen under Gorilla Glass 3, with optional always-on mode
specs.batteryAssumptions: Google's 'up to 7 days' assumes the always-on display OFF and SpO2 off; the spec sheet states both 'will require more frequent charging'. Full charge takes ~2 hours
specs.subscriptionModel: Optional in name, heavy in practice — Daily Readiness Score, the Sleep Score breakdown, the detailed Stress Management breakdown and the workout library all sit behind Google Health Premium. 3 months included
specs.waterRating: 5 ATM / 50 m to ISO 22810:2010 — Google notes water resistance 'decreases or is lost over time'
specs.ecgAfibStatus: ECG app via multipurpose electrical sensors plus PPG irregular-rhythm notifications. Fitbit's ECG feature is FDA-cleared in the US; Google's current Charge 6 spec sheet does not restate the clearance
specs.spo2Sensor: Yes — red and infrared sensors, overnight SpO2
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS 16.4+ or Android 11+, and setup requires a Google account
specs.chargerType: Proprietary magnetic cable shared with Charge 5 and Luxe; Google sells it as a standalone accessory (the Google Store listing did not render a price when checked)
specs.dataExport: Google Takeout export of the Google Health/Fitbit archive (JSON and CSV bundles)

pros: Genuine built-in GPS — the single spec that separates it from every other Fitbit band
Bluetooth heart-rate broadcast to treadmills, bikes and Peloton is rare at this price
Both S and L bands ship in the box rather than being a $30 upsell
ECG and EDA electrodes give it health hardware the cheaper bands physically lack
cons: Daily Readiness Score and the useful half of the sleep analysis are Google Health Premium features — $99.99/year once the 3-month trial lapses, up from Fitbit Premium's old $79.99
The 7-day figure assumes always-on display and SpO2 both off; turn either on and Google itself says to expect less
A Google account is mandatory to set the tracker up at all
Proprietary charging cable that fits only Charge 5, Charge 6 and Luxe
Wrist optical HR degrades badly above ~150bpm — peer-reviewed testing found Fitbit units underestimate HR during intense intervals
shortTagline: The only Fitbit band with real GPS — but the best metrics are a $99.99/year rental.

features: Up to 10 days per charge — the longest-lasting Fitbit band
Colour touchscreen with optional always-on mode
Overnight SpO2 and skin-temperature variation
Small and large bands included
5 ATM so it survives swimming

specs.gpsType: Connected GPS — borrows the paired phone's GPS. There is no GPS chip in the band, so no phone means no route or pace
specs.displayType: Colour touchscreen with optional always-on display (Google does not publish the panel size on the current store page)
specs.batteryAssumptions: 'Up to 10 days' with the always-on display off; Google states always-on 'may require more frequent charging'. Continuous HR is on by default
specs.subscriptionModel: Optional — steps, HR, sleep stages and the basic Sleep Score are free. The Stress Management Score breakdown, most mindfulness content, the Wellness Report PDF and the Gemini-powered coaching need Google Health Premium
specs.waterRating: 5 ATM / 50 m to ISO 22810:2010, shallow water only
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG electrodes. PPG-based irregular-rhythm notifications only
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS and Android; a Google account is required for setup
specs.chargerType: Proprietary clip-on magnetic charger, not shared with the Charge line
specs.dataExport: Google Takeout export of the Google Health/Fitbit archive (JSON and CSV bundles)

pros: Ten days between charges beats the Charge 6 by three and the Apple/Samsung watches by a week
Both band sizes in the box, and 5 ATM means you can swim in it
Cheapest route into the Fitbit/Google Health ecosystem with a real screen
Same free sleep-stage data as the Charge 6 for $60 less
cons: Connected GPS only — the phone has to come with you or the run has no distance or route
The 10-day claim collapses if you enable the always-on display, by Google's own admission
No ECG hardware and no exercise-equipment heart-rate broadcast
Yet another proprietary charger, and it is not the Charge 5/6/Luxe cable
Now four years old and outflanked by the newer, screenless Fitbit Air at the same price
shortTagline: Ten-day battery and a real screen for $99.95 — but the GPS is your phone's.

material: Polymer case with silicone band, replaceable in S/M and L sizes
features: Body Battery energy monitoring and all-day stress tracking
Pulse Ox on demand, all day or overnight
Physically replaceable bands in two sizes
Garmin Connect with nothing paywalled
Incident detection and Assistance when paired with a phone

specs.gpsType: Connected GPS — the band has no GPS chip and uses the paired phone's location for outdoor distance and route
specs.displayType: OLED touchscreen, 66% larger than the vívosmart 4 (Garmin's press release does not state the panel dimensions)
specs.batteryAssumptions: 'Up to 7 days' in smartwatch mode. Garmin does not publish a separate figure for all-day Pulse Ox enabled, which is the setting that drains it fastest
specs.subscriptionModel: None for anything on the device. Garmin Connect is free; the optional Garmin Connect+ tier adds AI summaries but gates nothing the vívosmart 5 measures
specs.waterRating: 5 ATM — Garmin rates it swim- and shower-proof
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG hardware and no AFib detection on this model — Garmin's ECG app is limited to its Venu/fenix lines
specs.spo2Sensor: Yes — Pulse Ox, spot-check, all-day or overnight
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS and Android via Garmin Connect
specs.dataExport: Garmin Connect exports individual activities as GPX/TCX/CSV, offers a full account data export, and has a documented developer API

pros: Nothing it measures is paywalled — Body Battery, stress, sleep and Pulse Ox are all free, forever
Best data portability in the category: per-activity GPX/TCX/CSV plus a documented API
Bands are genuinely user-replaceable and come in two wrist sizes
Garmin Connect's training and sleep history is deeper than anything Fitbit gives away free
cons: $149.99 for connected GPS only — the $159.95 Fitbit Charge 6 has a real GPS chip for $10 more
Four years old with no successor, and the screen is small and dim next to a $52 Xiaomi band
Garmin does not publish what all-day Pulse Ox does to the 7-day battery claim
No ECG, no AFib detection, no exercise-equipment heart-rate broadcast
Yet another proprietary clip charger
shortTagline: Nothing paywalled and the best data export in the category — but the GPS is your phone's.

material: Woven SuperKnit band with polymer sensor module
features: Recovery, Strain and Sleep scores computed from 24/7 HRV and heart rate
Sensor samples 26 times per second, 7% smaller module than 4.0
Wireless PowerPack charges the band on the wrist
Healthspan / WHOOP Age and hormonal-insight features on the Peak tier
No screen at all — nothing to glance at, nothing to distract

specs.gpsType: None — no GPS chip. Route and pace exist only if the phone comes with you
specs.displayType: None — screenless; the band shows nothing and every metric is app-only
specs.batteryAssumptions: WHOOP claims '4+ days' from the device itself. The advertised '14+ days' is the band PLUS the wireless PowerPack — which the Peak tier includes and the cheapest One tier does not
specs.subscriptionModel: Mandatory. WHOOP does not sell the hardware at any price — Peak is $239/year and the band comes with it. WHOOP states it stops collecting, uploading and analysing your data once the membership ends
specs.waterRating: WHOOP markets the band as swim-safe; no ATM or IP figure is published in the 5.0 launch materials
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG hardware on 5.0 — the ECG electrodes and the FDA-cleared ECG feature are exclusive to the WHOOP MG. 5.0 gets PPG-based irregular-heart-rhythm notifications
specs.spo2Sensor: Yes — blood oxygen, included on the Peak tier
specs.chargerType: Wireless PowerPack (Peak and Life tiers). The $199 One tier ships a basic wired charger and a certified pre-owned 5.0 rather than a new one
specs.dataExport: Member data download and a developer API while the membership is active; access to the archive follows the membership

pros: Best-in-class recovery and sleep modelling — the Strain/Recovery framework is still the one everyone else copies
26Hz sampling and a 7% smaller module make it genuinely comfortable to sleep in
The wireless PowerPack means you never take the band off to charge it
HSA/FSA eligible, which softens the annual cost for some US buyers
cons: There is no purchase price — you cannot own a WHOOP. Stop paying and the band stops collecting, uploading and analysing anything
$239/year for Peak means three years costs $717, more than four Fitbit Charge 6s
The $199 One tier quietly ships a certified pre-owned band and the old wired charger
No screen and no GPS chip: without your phone you get no pace, no route and no way to check anything mid-workout
Independent testing consistently finds wrist optical HR unreliable above ~150bpm, which is exactly where Strain is calculated
shortTagline: The best recovery analytics in wearables, rented for $239/year and never owned.

material: Woven SuperKnit band with polymer sensor module and ECG contacts
features: On-demand ECG readings with FDA-cleared AFib detection
Daily Blood Pressure Insights (wellness feature, not a cleared medical device)
Everything in the Peak tier plus Healthspan and hormonal insights
Wireless PowerPack included
Priority phone support

specs.gpsType: None — no GPS chip. Route and pace exist only if the phone comes with you
specs.displayType: None — screenless; every metric is app-only
specs.batteryAssumptions: '4+ days' from the band itself; the '14+ days' headline is the band plus the wireless PowerPack that the Life tier includes
specs.subscriptionModel: Mandatory and top-tier only — the MG hardware exists only inside the $359/year Life membership and is not sold separately
specs.waterRating: WHOOP markets the band as swim-safe; no ATM or IP figure is published in the launch materials
specs.ecgAfibStatus: FDA-cleared ECG and AFib detection. Blood Pressure Insights is NOT FDA-cleared — the FDA issued WHOOP a warning letter in July 2025 over marketing it without authorisation, and closed the letter in June 2026 only after WHOOP relabelled it as a wellness feature
specs.chargerType: Wireless PowerPack included at this tier
specs.dataExport: Member data download and a developer API while the membership is active

pros: One of the very few wrist wearables with an FDA-cleared ECG and AFib detection
Everything Peak offers plus longevity/Healthspan metrics and priority support
Wireless PowerPack included, so the band never leaves your wrist
HSA/FSA eligible
cons: $359/year, forever — the MG cannot be bought outright and stops working as a tracker when the membership lapses
The headline Blood Pressure Insights feature is explicitly not FDA-cleared and drew an FDA warning letter in July 2025
Early MG units suffered widely reported sensor failures within hours of setup in May 2025
No screen and no GPS chip despite costing more per year than most GPS running watches cost outright
The ECG contacts do not change the fact that Strain is still computed from wrist PPG, which degrades at high intensity
shortTagline: FDA-cleared ECG on a screenless band you never own, at $359 every single year.

material: Woven nylon strap with polymer sensor module
features: Screenless recovery tracking with no subscription of any kind
BioCharge readiness and PAI activity scoring in the Zepp app
10-day rated battery — Tom's Guide measured 12
27 sport modes including strength training and Hyrox
Roughly a third the first-year cost of a WHOOP Peak membership

specs.gpsType: None — no GPS chip. Outdoor workouts borrow the phone's GPS through the Zepp app
specs.displayType: None — screenless; all data is read in the Zepp app
specs.batteryAssumptions: Amazfit rates 10 days with continuous HR on; Tom's Guide got 12 days in review testing. Recharge takes under 2 hours
specs.subscriptionModel: None. Every metric the strap produces is free forever — this is the device's entire pitch against WHOOP
specs.waterRating: Amazfit markets it as sweat- and shower-safe; a formal ATM rating was not stated in the retail listings consulted
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG hardware and no AFib detection
specs.spo2Sensor: Yes — blood oxygen via the Zepp app
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS and Android via the Zepp app
specs.dataExport: Zepp syncs to Strava, Google Fit and Apple Health; Amazfit does not publish a documented bulk-export format

pros: $99.99 once versus $239/year — the same screenless recovery concept without the rental model
Beat its own 10-day rating in independent testing, hitting 12 days
Zepp pushes workouts to Strava, Google Fit and Apple Health without a paid tier
Comfortable enough to sleep in, which is where a screenless band earns its keep
cons: Automatic workout detection is unreliable — reviewers found it missed yoga entirely and invented short bike rides
No GPS chip and no screen: without the phone you have no pace, distance or route
Recovery modelling is less mature than WHOOP's, and the Zepp app is busier and less polished
Amazfit does not publish a documented bulk data export or a water-resistance rating
Proprietary magnetic charging clip with no standard alternative
shortTagline: A WHOOP-shaped band with no membership — the subscription trap's cheapest antidote.

material: Polymer case with silicone strap on a standard 22mm quick-release fitting
features: Built-in five-system GNSS with free downloadable offline maps
1.97-inch AMOLED — the largest screen in this comparison
14 days typical, 26 days in battery-saver mode
Standard 22mm straps, so replacements cost a few dollars
Bluetooth calling and Zepp Flow voice control

specs.gpsType: Built-in GNSS across five satellite systems, with free offline maps — no phone required for route or pace
specs.batteryAssumptions: Amazfit's 14 days is 'typical use'; battery-saver mode stretches to 26 days. Continuous GPS use and the always-on display are not covered by the 14-day figure. Full charge 1.5–2.5 hours
specs.subscriptionModel: None — every metric and the offline maps are free
specs.waterRating: 5 ATM / 50 m for up to 10 minutes
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG hardware and no AFib detection
specs.spo2Sensor: Yes — blood oxygen plus stress and sleep via BioTracker
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS and Android via the Zepp app (text reply is Android-only)
specs.chargerType: Proprietary magnetic charging cradle terminating in USB-C. Amazfit's US product page states a cable is not included as a sustainability measure — confirm box contents before buying
specs.dataExport: Zepp syncs to Strava, Google Fit and Apple Health; no documented bulk-export format

pros: Real multi-band GNSS and offline maps for $79.99 — half the price of the cheapest Fitbit with a GPS chip
14-day typical battery with a 1.97-inch AMOLED is a combination nothing else here matches
Standard 22mm quick-release straps, so replacements are a few dollars rather than $35
No subscription, no gated metrics, works with both iPhone and Android
cons: Amazfit's US page says no charging cable is included in the box — verify before you buy, because the cradle is proprietary
No ECG, no AFib detection and no FDA-cleared health feature of any kind
Zepp's recovery and sleep modelling is shallower than Garmin's or WHOOP's, and there is no documented bulk data export
Sits awkwardly between band and watch — it is 46mm, so it wears like a watch not a slim tracker
The 14-day claim does not survive regular GPS workouts or the always-on display
shortTagline: Real built-in GPS and 14-day battery for $79.99 — the connected-GPS trap's cheapest escape.

material: Aluminium alloy frame with TPU strap (ceramic, leather, metal and knit straps sold separately)
features: 1.72-inch AMOLED at 1500 nits — brighter than trackers costing three times as much
21 days of typical battery life
150+ sport modes and an electronic compass
5 ATM water resistance
15.95g without the strap

specs.gpsType: None — no GPS chip. Xiaomi's own spec sheet does not list GNSS; outdoor distance depends on the phone
specs.batteryAssumptions: Xiaomi publishes three figures: 21 days typical, 9 days with the always-on display, 8 days under heavy load. The 21-day headline assumes AOD off
specs.subscriptionModel: None — no paid tier exists for the Mi Fitness app
specs.waterRating: 5 ATM / 50 m to ISO 22810; Xiaomi explicitly excludes hot showers and saunas
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG hardware and no AFib detection
specs.spo2Sensor: Yes — blood oxygen and stress via the nine-axis sensor package
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS and Android via Mi Fitness, but US units are 'Global Version' grey imports with no US Xiaomi warranty channel
specs.dataExport: Not documented by Xiaomi — Mi Fitness syncs to Strava and Apple Health/Google Fit, but there is no published bulk export

pros: Three weeks of battery and a 1500-nit AMOLED for around $52
Genuinely nothing is paywalled — no premium tier exists at all
5 ATM and 15.95g make it the easiest band here to forget you are wearing
Huge choice of first-party straps including ceramic, leather and metal
cons: No GPS chip at all — Xiaomi does not even list GNSS on the spec sheet, so every outdoor distance is the phone's
US buyers get 'Global Version' imports; there is no US Xiaomi warranty or support channel behind them
The 21-day figure drops to 9 days the moment you turn on the always-on display
No documented way to bulk-export your own data out of Mi Fitness
Sleep and recovery analysis is shallow compared with Garmin, Polar or WHOOP
shortTagline: Three weeks of battery and a brilliant screen for $52 — with zero GPS and grey-import support.

features: Aluminium body — unusual at this price
1.6-inch AMOLED, 45% wider than the Fit2
13 days rated with the always-on display off
5 ATM plus IP68 dust and water resistance
Fall detection and SOS via the paired phone

specs.gpsType: None — no GPS chip. It uses the paired phone's location; without a phone it estimates distance from the accelerometer and reviewers measured it undermeasuring a 5km track by 50m or more
specs.displayType: 1.6-inch AMOLED touchscreen with optional always-on mode
specs.batteryAssumptions: Samsung's 13 days is explicitly 'with Always On Display turned off (default setting)'. Independent testing under moderate-to-heavy use returned roughly 7–10 days
specs.waterRating: 5 ATM (50 m for 10 minutes) plus IP68
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG hardware and no AFib detection — Samsung's ECG is restricted to Galaxy Watch models paired with a Galaxy phone
specs.phoneCompatibility: Android only. There is no iOS app for the Fit3, and setup is smoothest on a Samsung phone
specs.chargerType: Proprietary pogo-pin cable; no wall adapter is included in the box
specs.dataExport: Samsung Health offers a personal-data download; third-party sync generally needs Health Connect on Android

pros: Aluminium body and a 1.6-inch AMOLED for $59.99
5 ATM plus IP68 is the most thorough water/dust rating in the budget tier
Nothing is paywalled and Samsung Health is a mature, free app
Fall detection and SOS are rare features at this price
cons: Android only — there is no iPhone app, which rules the Fit3 out entirely for iOS users
No GPS chip, and phone-free distance estimation was measured undermeasuring a 5km track by 50m+
The 13-day claim is with the always-on display off; real-world use lands nearer 7–10 days
Proprietary pogo-pin charging cable and no wall adapter in the box
Best-behaved on a Samsung phone; on other Android handsets setup is clumsier
shortTagline: An aluminium AMOLED band for $59.99 — as long as you never want to use an iPhone.

material: Polymer sensor module with textile wristband; S/M and M/L bands included
features: Screenless 24/7 tracking with Polar's Precision Prime optical sensor
SleepWise alertness prediction and Nightly Recharge recovery scoring
No subscription — every feature from day one
Both S/M and M/L bands included in the box
Four weeks of onboard memory if you leave your phone behind

specs.gpsType: None — no GPS chip. The Polar Flow app can use the phone's GPS when you start an outdoor session manually
specs.displayType: None — screenless; everything is read in Polar Flow
specs.batteryAssumptions: Polar rates up to 8 days with continuous HR active; the band holds about four weeks of data if it goes unsynced
specs.subscriptionModel: None. Polar states full access to every feature from day one with no monthly fee — the explicit anti-WHOOP position
specs.waterRating: WR30 — Polar rates it for bathing and swimming, a weaker rating than the 5 ATM bands here
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG hardware and no AFib detection
specs.spo2Sensor: Not listed by Polar for the Loop — the sensor package is optical HR, HRV and accelerometer
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS and Android via Polar Flow

pros: Polar's sports-science pedigree — Nightly Recharge and SleepWise — with no subscription attached
Two band sizes in the box, so the fit problem is solved at purchase
Real data portability: TCX/GPX export, account export and a documented API
Two-year warranty, double the Fitbit and Amazfit norm
cons: $199.99 for a screenless band with no GPS chip and no SpO2 — the $99.99 Amazfit Helio Strap does the same job
WR30 rather than 5 ATM, the weakest water rating in this comparison
8 days is the shortest battery life of any screenless band here
No ECG, no AFib detection, no FDA-cleared health feature
Polar Flow's interface is dated next to WHOOP's and Google Health's

material: Stainless steel case, Gorilla Glass, fluoroelastomer strap
features: Hybrid analogue dial with a 0.63-inch grayscale OLED sub-display
Up to a month between charges
24/7 heart rate with high/low alerts and cycle tracking
Stainless steel case at 37mm — the only metal-cased device here
HSA/FSA eligible

specs.gpsType: Connected GPS at best — the Amazon listing advertises 'Connected GPS' using the phone, while Withings' own shop spec sheet does not list GPS at all. Sources conflict; either way there is no GPS chip in the watch
specs.displayType: Analogue hands plus a 0.63-inch grayscale OLED sub-display (282 PPI)
specs.batteryAssumptions: Sources conflict: Withings' own shop page claims up to 35 days, while the Amazon listing title and launch coverage say 30 days. No SpO2 sensor is drawing power
specs.subscriptionModel: Optional — Withings+ adds cardiologist ECG review, the AI Health Assistant, NutriCare and Readiness scoring. One month is included. Withings does not publish the Withings+ price on its US product or subscription pages
specs.annualSubscriptionUsd: Not published on Withings' US Withings+ page
specs.ecgAfibStatus: No ECG on the Light — Withings reserves ECG and AFib detection for ScanWatch 2 and Nova. The cardiologist ECG review sold under Withings+ therefore does not apply to this model
specs.spo2Sensor: No — Withings explicitly omits the SpO2 sensor on the Light
specs.phoneCompatibility: iOS and Android via Withings Health Mate
specs.dataExport: Health Mate offers a full account data export in CSV, and Withings publishes a developer API

pros: A month or more per charge, by far the longest run time in this comparison
Stainless steel and real analogue hands — it passes as a watch, not a fitness band
CSV account export and a public API make your data genuinely portable
Two-year warranty and HSA/FSA eligibility
cons: $249.95 buys no ECG, no SpO2 and no GPS chip — the 'Light' name is doing a lot of work
Sources conflict on both battery life (30 vs 35 days) and whether connected GPS is supported at all
The Withings+ features most people want, including cardiologist ECG review, need hardware this model does not have
Withings does not publish the Withings+ price on its US pages, so the real cost of ownership is unclear at purchase
The 0.63-inch grayscale sub-display shows very little at a glance
shortTagline: A month of battery in a steel watch case — with no ECG, no SpO2 and no GPS chip.
